skeptic.summary:
I could not spot-check anything. The web-search budget for this session is used up (200 of 200 calls), and the first two queries were refused. Every flag therefore rests on evidence already in the catalogue: its own descriptions, its verification marks, and the task's inclusion rule. I made no new factual claims except well-established ones: Christ is Passing By has 18 homilies, The Way of the Cross has fourteen Stations, the Navarre Bible commentary comes from the University of Navarra, Álvaro del Portillo succeeded St Josemaría, and 'Our Lives in His Hands' concerns Tomás Alvira and Paquita, whose cause is open.

What I found:
(1) Author spellings are inconsistent. The list uses five forms for Escrivá, Fernandez/Fernández, Suarez/Suárez, Coverdale with and without 'F.', and Stenson with and without 'B.'. All are normalised to St Josemaría Escrivá, Francis Fernández, Federico Suárez, John F. Coverdale and James B. Stenson.
(2) One misattribution: the Critical-Historical Edition of The Way listed Pedro Rodríguez as author. He is the editor.
(3) Six doubtful items whose own descriptions attest only the US Scepter Publishers edition fail the task's rule for US titles. They are marked drop unless a scepter.uk or Amazon UK (Scepter UK) listing is found: Conversations, Time for God, Thirsting for Prayer, The Narrow Gate, Pocket New Testament, Man and Values.
(4) Descriptions that record publisher, format or provenance instead of content were rewritten: Christ Is Passing By, The Way of the Cross, Navarre Bible, Christ on Earth, Father the Family Protector, The Gospel in the Home, Successful Fathers.
(5) Title and subtitle fixes: 'Foundation' vs 'Foundational' Letters, the missing article on The Four Last Things, and lowercase words in two titles.

No duplicates found, and no entries from other publishers such as Hodder's Sceptre. All descriptions are within 22 words.

These entries stay marked doubtful for UK provenance, but I did not flag them, because their descriptions do not tie them to the US edition: The Way/Furrow/The Forge one-volume, Interior Freedom Study Guide, Saxum, Berglar's Opus Dei, Simon Peter, Compass, Lifeline, Covenanted Happiness, The Gospel in the Home.

Gaps, which I could not add as flags: 'In Love with the Church' is named in the brief as a Scepter UK Escrivá title but is missing from the catalogue. Letters 1 and 2 of the Foundational Letters series are also absent while 3 and 4 are present. Christ on Earth carries a Sinag-Tala ISBN, so it should also appear on the Sinag-Tala site.
